label: H3 Live Action - Signature Combat
useWhen: named characters must fight with recognizable move ownership
powers or weapons must drive choreography instead of decorate it
contact, mass and reaction must be readable in live action

durationContract.rule: one named move or counter and its complete physical reaction; no filler exchange

required: approved first, contact and last anchors with SHA-256 and approval scope
identity matrix and combat identity matrix for every fighter
one named signature move with fixed owner and forbidden substitutions
anticipation, propulsion, contact, displacement, reaction and recovery
effect or weapon lifecycle attached to the correct body, object and character
controlContract.intermediateAnchor: always required at the signature contact or technical pose
controlContract.motion: prompt guided between locked action states; model freedom is limited to connective micro-movement

forbidden: MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo mixed into the FL2VA graph
power transferred to the wrong fighter
detached decorative aura, beam, fire or particles without physical cause
camera shake, RIFE or Foley used to counterfeit impact
RIFE or upscale before source approval

promptContract.language: English except original dialogue and visible text
promptContract.timelineRule: Write one exact named exchange over 0-30%, 30-70% and 70-100%; useful body and camera motion continues through the last interval.
promptContract.moveRule: The declared move owner, mechanism, silhouette and outcome are immutable. H3 may solve only connective micro-movement.
promptContract.physicsRule: Show anticipation, planted force or airborne propulsion, visible contact or evasion, center-of-mass displacement, opponent reaction and active recovery.
promptContract.effectRule: Declare source, body/object attachment, onset, trajectory, contact response, decay and environmental consequence. The effect may not jump owners or replace body mechanics.
promptContract.readabilityRule: The camera must show the attack line and consequence; no cutaway, occlusion or shake may hide the contact beat.
